utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is obviously a protected witness; am I right? The hearing is public.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the protected witness should be granted a pseudonym and image distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The pseudonym is DO, I believe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is a victim who intends --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Don't say the name. Be careful. This is a public session, so don't say the name. I'm not asking you for the same thing twice. Even though your summary is very, in fact, short, don't go into any further details. You don't have to make the summary. All right. This is Witness DO who is going to be brought into the courtroom immediately so that we don't waste any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. I merely wanted to explain the reasons for this. It was a case for the protection and security of the witness. That is why we asked for these additional protective measures. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness DO, I'm sorry I have to call you that. Do you hear me? I am speaking to the witness who has just come into the courtroom. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First, we're going to ask that you identify your name on a piece of paper which is going to be given to you, but don't state your name. The registrar is going to give you the piece of paper. Don't say it, but is that, in fact, your name? Just say "Yes" or "No."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're going to take an oath, while remaining standing, in your language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness DO. You may be seated. You are covered by protective measures, that is, this is a public hearing, but anything which would allow your identity to be revealed will be hidden. I think that is the face and the voice, as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I think the request from the Defence was a pseudonym and face distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Your testimony will be public, but if there are parts in it which should not be revealed, you can be assured that either the Prosecution or the Defence counsel or the Judges will ask that it be a completely closed session. Witness DO, you may speak without fear. As I say, you have been covered by protective measures. You are before Judges and you can express yourself freely. Tonight it will not be very long, it will give you some time to rest and to get used to being where you are, and then we're going to sit now for about 20 or 25 minutes. We will begin with the Defence because you are a Defence witness. Let me remind you that the accused is in the courtroom, that's Colonel Blaskic, today General Blaskic. The questions will be asked first by Mr. Nobilo and then the Prosecution will have some questions, and then finally the Judges. Mr. Nobilo, proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May we move into private session for one or two minutes to determine the CV of the witness, so we shall be excluding the public completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right, now we are in a closed session. (Closed session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your first home where you lived with your husband and your children, on the 18th of April, 1993, you left that home. Tell us whether the whole family left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the whole family went in the morning at 5.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave alone or did most of your Croat neighbours leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of my Croat neighbours left, as many Croats as there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for your departure, for leaving your home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that morning, there was firing. We knew what happened at Dusina, we were frightened, and before that, they would come in vehicles and fuck our Ustashe mothers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Muslims, the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Witness DO, when you answer the questions, if you don't mind, please turn to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It did not go into the transcript. Did I hear you correctly when you said that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina would curse you and fuck your Ustasha mothers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you leave that new village? We're not going to mention the name. We mentioned it a moment ago while we were in closed session. But when did you leave that particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grahovcici, at the beginning of June, that's when we left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you leave that village, the village you lived in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there for a time, and then there was shelling. Grahovcici was shelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who shelled Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you went to the Vitez municipality. Don't mention the name of the village, but please just tell us, the place you lived in, how far is it from the town of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is one kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I should now like to hand around a map for you to be able to see the exact locality, but I think it would be a good idea not to make this map public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So long as this is given to the Prosecution as well, but I think you were going to do so, so that's no problem. Do you have that, Mr. Harmon, that is, the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm awaiting its arrival. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D455. D454 will be kept for the document which has been given which, at the request of the Trial Chamber, will be submitted by the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness DO, in the middle of this circle, is that where the house is located where you were put up as a refugee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: For the transcript, the circles in the right-hand corner are not relevant. They are there as an error. So only the circle in the middle of the map is relevant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the situation like? Were there a lot of refugees? How many people lived in the house? Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were five of us living in the house, two children, my husband, myself, and my husband's aunt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the other houses in Vitez, were there a lot of refugees at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were about 70 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that particular village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you came to that village, you lived in Vitez. How many of you lived in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nineteen of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there a lot of refugees in Vitez as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were a lot of refugees. We had no other choice. We had to go into a house which was empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you come to the village that is located in the circle on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in August.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, was it a large village? How many houses did the village have, the village that you found yourselves in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not a large village. It was a small settlement below Sivrino Selo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many houses could there have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 15 houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the refugees, were there locals living there who had been there before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were locals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was the frontline between the Croats and the Muslims from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ten (sic) metres, not more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fifty metres from your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should tell the Trial Chamber that the name of the village is in the summary that we submitted to you, so we don't want to mention it in public session. You said that 50 metres away from your houses was the frontline. Who held the frontline?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which were these people? It was the people who were already there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you trying to tell me it was the locals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the locals who had already lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We shall be talking about an event which occurred on the 9th of January, 1994. Tell me, just before that event, did some other soldiers come to your village, apart from those who had already lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, no one came. There were the locals who were already there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the members of the Munja, did they come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Munja men were staying at a house. They were not at the frontline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, so they were staying in houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were staying beneath the house where I was staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Munja were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, nine of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were members of the HVO; right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please describe to the Court what happened on the morning of January 9th, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the evening, we went to bed, that is to say, that was the evening of the 8th. And in the morning between 4.30 and 5.00, we were awakened. I don't know what time it was. It was between 4.30 and 5.00 a.m., and they said, "Ustasha surrender. Allah-u-ekber." We heard different voices, and we were terrified. My husband, my children, his aunt, and I, we got dressed in a hurry into whatever clothes we could find, and then we went downstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to your children and your husband's aunt, you mentioned your husband. Was he in the army, in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, before he was, but at that time, he was not at the frontline. He was at home. And why? He had had a traffic accident. A gentleman called Mirko Samija got killed. He was walking along the road. A sniper hit him and threw him 15 metres away, so he could not really function. He spent three days at the medical centre, and since there were a lot of people at the medical centre, they sent him home. He had to use crutches. His legs were black underneath the knees, so he was not capable of walking without crutches.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. It is not quite clear in the transcript how your husband got hit by this car. I shall try to sum up what you have said, and then you tell me whether this is correct. The driver of a car was hit by a sniper, and he got killed as he was driving, at the wheel. And then after he died, his car skidded and hit your husband; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, my husband was walking by, and he had a wheelbarrow, and he was carrying flour in it or whatever we needed. So it was this dead man who was still at the steering wheel, and then the car hit my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband have any weapon at home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Court what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, we went downstairs and we tried to get out through the windows, and whenever we would speak to these people, we would say, "Can we get out? We are not Ustasha." They were screaming, they were hollering, and they were throwing things at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The BH army. I just managed to say, "Let us try to escape through the door." I was the first to get out, and then the two children followed me. My third daughter was not there, my oldest daughter, and the two young children were with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your children were ten and seven; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please try to slow down, and do not mention the names of your children, please, and do not mention the name of your husband either later on, okay? We are talking about your husband and your 10-year-old and 7-year-old children, but try not to mention any names. The names you mentioned will be deleted from the transcript by the registrar, but it is going to make everybody's job much easier if you simply do not mention names, please. Could you please describe what happened afterwards? You were fleeing from your houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I waited there, and I realised that my husband and his aunt did not catch up with us. The main road was nearby, and we took the main road, and there were others who were escaping from there, and I was there together with them, and we reached Impregnacija. When we reached Impregnacija, that was where a man was there at the door. It was a small area, and the BH army shelled us. We waited there for two or three hours, and then I continued towards Vitez. I got there, and my husband's sister lived in the yellow building, and that is where I stayed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, you and your two children managed to escape from the village before the assault of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what happened to your husband? Did your husband manage to escape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband did not. On the 21st of January, I came to see -- I mean, the Red Cross would help me, and I was supposed to recognise my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we move on to the recognition, could you tell me whether you received information from some women that he was taken prisoner, that he was alive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we received that kind of information. There were ten women who were taken prisoner and one child, and somebody said that my husband was a prisoner there too; however, my husband was not a prisoner there. On the 21st of January, I could not go there and see whether it was my husband or not. They brought him to the house in a coffin. I did not see him. UNPROFOR came then, and they were taking pictures, and whoever wishes to see this can.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before we come to a description of what you have seen, I would like to ask the registrar to have this document distributed. This is a photograph, and we are going to see it on the video monitor later. Mr. President, there is just one photograph there, and we shall use the video monitor later. I talked to the witness, and she is prepared to look at it. Let me just explain. She received half of her husband's body. First she received one half of her husband's body, and then she received the other half, and now you are going to see the first half that she got. Is the witness prepared to have a look at this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D456.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Madam, could you describe the situation when your husband's body was delivered to you? What did people tell you? What did he look like, and what did you see later on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told me that only the upper half of my husband's body was in the coffin. UNPROFOR were taking pictures, and I saw later on television that this was my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The picture that you have in front of you now, is that a reflection of what you saw on television, that is to say, the upper part of the body, and in the middle, one can see the spine a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bury this half of your husband's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, immediately during the day. A month later, not exactly a month later, on the 25th, the lower part of the body arrived. That I saw with my very own eyes, and that I recognised, that that was my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what did you see, and how did you recognise that part of the body as being your husband's?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised it. There were his trousers, his tracksuit, and the clothes, I recognised the clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go and bury the other part in the same place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we bought another coffin. This other coffin was useless, and we took the upper part of the body and this other part, and we put it altogether and buried it altogether. If I can remember well, this was the 15th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps we could stop at this point, Mr. President, if you think the time is right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, these are dreadful, dreadful details. There is no hearing tomorrow, so that under the supervision of the Witnesses and Victims Unit, we can ask the witness to try to relax a little bit. I know these are very painful memories. We will see each other again at 2.15 on Wednesday. The Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.43 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of December, 1998 at 2.15 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: Pages 15734 to 15809 redacted – in closed session
